Action Plan:
1. Call emergency services (999) immediately for suspected anaphylaxis and arrange urgent transfer to ED.  
2. Take any available oral antihistamine while awaiting ambulance arrival.  
3. Ensure a responsible adult remains with the patient until hand-over to paramedics.  
4. Post-discharge: arrange review with GP/allergy clinic for prescription and teaching of adrenaline auto-injector, detailed food allergy work-up, and emergency action plan.  
5. Review asthma control and ensure adequate supply of salbutamol inhaler at follow-up.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Rapidly enlarging upper-lip swelling beginning ~30 min after eating prawn soup at 19:00 today.  
• Symptom progression: Swelling continues to enlarge; associated throat tightness, difficulty breathing, chest discomfort (uncertain), and dizziness.  
• Past episodes: Similar facial swelling + breathing difficulty after Chinese food ~1 year ago; hospitalised for severe allergic reaction at age 6 (mother’s report).  
• Past medical history: Asthma; known peanut allergy.  
• Medications: Salbutamol inhaler PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented); “occasional” antihistamines (names/doses not documented).  
• Allergies: Peanuts (IgE mediated); shellfish/prawn suspected (new).  
• Social: Lives with mother; friend/social outings; no other details provided.

Objective:
• Visual: Marked swelling of upper lip observed on video.  
• Respiratory: Patient reports dyspnoea and throat tightness; audible concern noted.  
• Dizziness reported.  
• No formal vitals or other system examinations documented.  
• No investigations performed prior to ambulance call.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute lip swelling with respiratory compromise
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to shellfish (prawn) – DDx item “IgE-mediated anaphylaxis triggered by shellfish (High)”.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     • Isolated allergic angioedema to shellfish (Medium) – less likely given systemic features.  
     • Hereditary angioedema (Low-Medium) – food trigger argues against.  
     • Infectious lip cellulitis (Low).  
   - Investigations planned: To be completed in ED (airway assessment, vitals, serum tryptase, allergy testing after recovery).  
   - Treatment planned: Immediate ambulance transfer; administer oral antihistamine while waiting; expect intramuscular adrenaline, oxygen, IV fluids in ED; post-discharge prescription of adrenaline auto-injector and written emergency plan.  
   - Relevant referrals: Allergy/immunology clinic for definitive testing and education.

2. Asthma (background)
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Intermittent asthma, currently stable but exacerbation risk during anaphylaxis.
   - Differential diagnosis: n/a (established condition).
   - Investigations planned: None acutely; spirometry at follow-up if indicated.
   - Treatment planned: Continue salbutamol inhaler PRN; review inhaler technique and need for preventer at follow-up.
   - Relevant referrals: Consider asthma nurse/clinic review post-discharge.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: No documented vital signs, full medication list, full allergy list (drug/environmental), or detailed asthma history.  
• Transcript & DDx conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational filler, no major inaudible sections.
